chunks: From him, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali Al-Khazzaz, and Ali ibn Al-Hakam, from Muthanna Al-Hannat, from Zurarah ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked: A woman left behind her husband, her mother, her maternal siblings, and her paternal-maternal siblings. He said: 'For her husband is half, for her mother is one-sixth, and for the maternal siblings is one-third, and the paternal-maternal siblings are excluded.'

Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan said: These narrations contradict the truth and are not acted upon by the entire sect, because it is known among them that with the mother, no siblings (brothers or sisters) inherit, which we have explained previously. The explanation for these narrations is that they are carried on a type of precautionary dissimulation (taqiyyah) to align with the views of the general public (Sunni). It is also possible that what came regarding permission for us to take from them according to their beliefs, as they take from us, applies, and it is only forbidden for one of us to take from another contrary to the truth, which is indicated by this.
9. What was narrated by: Ali ibn Al-Hasan ibn Fadhl, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Hakim, from Jamil ibn Darradj, from Abdullah ibn Muhrij, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He said: I asked him: A man left behind his daughter and his paternal-maternal sister. He said: 'All the wealth belongs to his daughter, and the paternal-maternal sister gets nothing.'

I said: We have need for this, and the deceased man is from these people (non-Shia), and his sister is a believing, knowledgeable woman. He said: 'Then take half for her. Take from them what they take from you in their sunnah, their judgments, and their rulings.'
He said: So I mentioned that to Zurarah, who said: Indeed, upon what Ibn Muhrij brought is a light. Take them by your right in their rulings and their sunnah, as they take from you in it.
10. And - from him, from Ayub ibn Nuh

He said: I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) asking him: Do we take in the rulings of the non-Shia what they take from us in their rulings or not? He wrote (peace be upon him): 'It is permissible for you to do so if your school of thought in it is precautionary dissimulation (taqiyyah) from them and diplomacy (mudarayah').

key_terms.أَحْكَامِهِمْ: Their rulings; legal judgments made by non-Shia authorities.
key_terms.التَّقِيَّة: Precautionary dissimulation; concealing one's true beliefs or rulings to avoid harm or align with others.
key_terms.الْمُدَارَاة: Diplomacy or conciliation; dealing with others gently to maintain harmony or authority.
key_terms.سُنَّتِهِمْ: Their sunnah; their established practices and traditions in legal matters.
key_terms.مَذَاهِبِ الْعَامَّةِ: The schools of thought of the general public (Sunni Muslims).

ai.seo_question: How do Shia jurists reconcile the hadith of Zurarah regarding sibling inheritance with the established Shia ruling that siblings do not inherit with the mother?
ai.summary: This passage from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the jurisprudential debate regarding the exclusion of paternal-maternal siblings (*ikhwah lil-umm wa lil-ab*) when the mother is alive, contrasting Zurarah’s narration with the dominant Shia view. Shaykh al-Tusi notes that while the narration is considered contrary to the established truth, it is often attributed to *taqiyyah* to align with Sunni methodology, or serves as a basis for *al-akhthu minahum* (taking from them) in their own legal affairs. The text concludes with Imam al-Rida’s confirmation that applying non-Shia rulings to them is permissible if it serves the purpose of *taqiyyah* or *mudarrahah* (pragmatic accommodation).
